subject: FalconData throughput regression — ownership, verification plan, and follow-through
messages:
From: Priya Sethi <priya@falcondata.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, FalconData Ops <ops@falcondata.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden throughput regression impacting batch inference (FalconData)

Markus / Redwood team —

We saw a sharp drop in throughput starting ~08:43 PDT today across our busiest inference routes (batch-sizing: 64, p95 latency upx3, error spike 5% 5xx). This is hitting our pipeline processing windows and causing back-pressure into downstream ETL.

What we need immediately:
- Confirmation you’ve received the alert and assigned an on-call owner.
- A tentative ETA for a remediation or mitigation step we can apply (even if temporary).
- We’ve attached log snippets and request IDs.

Attaching: falcondata-incident-logs.tar.gz (excerpts included)

—Priya
Priya Sethi
Head of Platform Engineering, FalconData
priya@falcondata.com
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sethi <priya@falcondata.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput regression impacting batch inference (FalconData)

Priya — thanks for the heads up and the logs. We have an on-call owner assigned (Rishi) and a small mitigation playbook in motion.

Immediate steps we’re taking:
- Rishi's team will roll a 10% reduction to batch size and enable a short-lived prefix cache to drop token-level compute for hot keys (15 min rollout window).
- We’ll collect KV cache metrics and token CPU/GPU utilization and share within 30m.
- We’ll open an incident RCA thread and schedule an executive readout if the regression persists beyond 24h.

Can you confirm whether you can tolerate a 10% throughput reduction from Redwood in the next 30 min while we validate?

I’ve cc’d Laura for commercial impact and Grace to track escalation comms.

—Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Priya Sethi <priya@falcondata.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput regression impacting batch inference (FalconData)

Priya / team — quick status and preliminary RCA (short version):

What we observed:
- A subtle regression in kernel scheduling triggered by a new autoscaler behavior on one Dedicated pool during the 08:30–09:00 window (mismatched seq-length histogram -> suboptimal kernel choice).
- This produced elevated tail latency for long sequences, which cascaded into queue buildup and request backpressure.

Actions taken (applied 09:15–09:30):
- Forced fallback to conservative kernel selection for the affected pool (mitigates p95).
- Reduced default batch size from 64->57 for FalconData routes as a temporary step.
- Captured full run traces and exported logs (attached: falcondata-rca-draft.md).

Open corrective items (proposed):
1) Short-term (48h): automated sequence-length skews detection + auto-fallback to conservative kernels. Owner: Rishi. ETA: 48h for deploy to staging, 72h for canary in prod.
2) Mid-term (2 weeks): add histogram-aware kernel selection in the scheduler (perf engineering). Owner: Performance team (TBD).
3) Runbook/update: add clear rollback/play for autoscaler changes and a one-click fallback for customers. Owner: Monica.

I’ll continue to monitor — attaching the draft RCA and runbook delta.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Attachments: falcondata-rca-draft.md, runbook-delta.patch
From: Priya Sethi <priya@falcondata.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: FalconData Ops <ops@falcondata.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput regression impacting batch inference (FalconData)

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the quick mitigation. We saw improvement after the fallback and batch-size reduction; p95 returned toward baseline but we're still seeing intermittent 502s during peak windows (09:00–10:30 PDT).

Questions/asks:
- Can you share the exact verification queries/metrics you’ll use to sign off the fix? We need those for our internal postmortem.
- We’ll need a timeline for the short-term automation and whether that will be retrofitted to our Dedicated pool without disruption.
- Please include a proposed commercial gesture for the SLA miss (FalconData account team will coordinate).

We can do a quick sync this afternoon if that helps.

—Priya
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sethi <priya@falcondata.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden throughput regression impacting batch inference (FalconData) — mutual action plan

Priya / team — outlining the mutual action plan and owners so we have a single source of truth. We’ll also prepare an exec readout if you’d like one (we recommend 48–72h after stabilization).

Mutual action plan (MAP):
- Verification checklist (Rishi, Monica):
  * p95 latency for FalconData routes <= baseline +5% over 3 consecutive peak windows (query: redis.kv.cache_hit_ratio, serving.p95_ms, gpu.util_percent).
  * 5xx rate <0.5% over 24h.
  * No request queue growth >10% compared to baseline during peak.
  ETA: monitoring dashboards and alert rules by 24h.

- Technical fixes:
  1) Short-term automation (detect histo skew & auto-fallback). Owner: Rishi. Due: 2026-08-24 EOD (staging); canary 2026-08-26.
  2) Scheduler improvement (histogram-aware kernel selection). Owner: Performance team (Monica to coordinate). Due: 2026-09-06 (PR and perf test plan).
  3) Runbook + rollback one-click. Owner: Monica. Due: 2026-08-25.

- Commercial/ops:
  * Laura to propose account-level credit for any SLA window exceeding agreed thresholds and prepare a scoped note for the Customer Success/Finance review.
  * Executive readout proposed: Thu 2026-08-26 10:00 AM PT (tentative).

Action owners and next steps:
- Rishi: Implement automation in staging and share verification queries (by 08/24 EOD).
- Monica: Publish runbook delta and coordinate perf team (by 08/25).
- Laura: Draft commercial credit proposal and coordinate with FalconData (by 08/25).
- Markus / Grace: handle exec invites and comms.

Please reply here to confirm owners and that these dates are acceptable. I’ll convert to a Jira epic (SUP-13287) and link to the HubSpot ticket.

—Laura Bennett
Sr. Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sethi <priya@falcondata.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2026 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput regression impacting batch inference (FalconData) — ownership and closure criteria

Team — thanks for the fast coordination. Confirming commitments:

- Rishi: short-term automation deploy to staging by EOD 08/24; canary target 08/26. Verification queries and dashboard links (SUP-13287) must be posted to the Jira ticket once ready.
- Monica: runbook drop and rollback script by 08/25; coordinate with ops for a non-disruptive rollout to Dedicated pools.
- Laura: commercial credit proposal and customer note by 08/25; prepare for exec readout on 08/26.
- Markus / Grace: exec readout invite will go out 08/25; readout agenda: timeline, RCA summary, mitigation validation, commercial next steps.

Closure criteria for the RCA (must be met before thread archived):
1) Verification checklist satisfied for 72h sliding window.
2) Automation deployed to canary and validated (no regressions observed).
3) Runbook published and shared with FalconData.
4) Commercial remediation agreed (credit or service extension) and documented in HubSpot.

Priya — please confirm your acceptance of the MAP and closure criteria; if accepted we’ll treat this as the canonical path to close the incident. If you want the exec readout earlier, suggest a time and we’ll adjust.

—Markus
VP, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
